seoDescription: Acclaimed actress Monica Bellucci reflects on the pivotal moments and iconic roles that have defined her extensive career. From her early work with Francis Ford Coppola in 'Bram Stoker's Dracula' to her breakout performance in 'Malèna,' Bellucci shares insights into her craft. She discusses the challenges of her role in the controversial 'Irréversible,' her experience joining 'The Matrix' franchise, and the revolutionary significance of playing the oldest Bond 'lady' in 'Spectre' at age 50.

summary:
## Career Beginnings
- Transitioned from fashion to acting after being discovered by Roman Coppola and cast by **Francis Ford Coppola** in *Bram Stoker's Dracula* (1992).
- Her first major American role was in *Under Suspicion* (2000) alongside **Gene Hackman** and **Morgan Freeman**.

## Malèna (2000)
- Director **Giuseppe Tornatore** conceived the role with Bellucci in mind years before filming.
- The character of Malèna communicates primarily through **body language**, a key tool for actors.
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The film depicts the brutal treatment of a woman desired by men but hated by other women in a male-dominated society. Bellucci notes the character only regains respect when she returns with her husband, highlighting the societal structure of the time.
- Bellucci felt safe filming the violent sequences due to careful **choreography** and a protective director.

## Irréversible (2002)
- Described as both the **most violent film** she's made and also **very poetic**.
- The infamous assault scene was shot like a **choreographed dance**, ensuring her safety despite its brutal on-screen appearance.
> [!TIP]
> The film was technically innovative, using **20-minute long sequence shots**. This allowed for extended, uninterrupted acting performances similar to theater.

## The Matrix Franchise (2003)
- Bellucci played **Persephone** in *The Matrix Reloaded* and *The Matrix Revolutions*.
- A prior connection with **Keanu Reeves** (from *Dracula*) helped her feel more comfortable joining the established cast.
- Her character is based on the Greek mythological figure, existing between two worlds, and needed to be portrayed as mysterious, dangerous, and sensual.

## The Passion of the Christ (2004)
- She actively pursued the role of **Mary Magdalene** after meeting the film's costume designer.
- Bellucci views Mary Magdalene as a symbol of **humanity**, someone grappling with faith and events larger than herself.

## Spectre (2015)
- At age 50, she became the **oldest "Bond lady"** (Lucia Sciarra).
- Initially, she humorously thought she was being considered for the role of **M**.
> [!NOTE]
> Bellucci considers her casting **revolutionary**, reflecting a new era where mature women have a greater impact in society and film, and their desirability is not tied to youth.

## Mozart in the Jungle (2016)
- This marked her first TV series and a reunion with producer **Roman Coppola**.
- She played an opera singer, requiring her to work very hard on **lip-syncing** perfectly in multiple languages (German, Italian, English).
- The character, Alessandra, is obsessed with her fading voice and afraid of aging, but is saved by her **childish nature**.

## Call My Agent! (2018)
- She played a fictionalized, "larger than life" version of herself.
- The role was a refreshing chance to do **comedy**, a departure from her many dramatic films.
> [!TIP]
> Bellucci emphasizes the importance for an actor to maintain **distance** from their work and to be able to laugh at themselves, which this role allowed her to do.

## Beetlejuice Beetlejuice (2024)
- She plays **Dolores**, the bride of Beetlejuice, in the Tim Burton film.
- She describes the characters' connection as a "poison love," united by their **dark souls**.
- She highlights the great on-set chemistry, particularly the long-standing rapport between **Tim Burton** and **Michael Keaton**.

## Core Philosophy
- **Passion** and **synergy** are the driving forces behind her career. She believes that if you truly want something and fight for it, it will happen.
transcription:
## From Fashion to Film: Early Career

My agent called me and told me Sam Mendes wanted to meet you for James Bond and I was 50 at the time, the oldest Bond lady ever. 

Hi, I'm Monica Bellucci and this is the timeline of my career. 

Obviously, Henry has talked to us about your marriage, how you wish you had married a younger man, someone closer to your own age like Paco. 

You're saying Henry is jealous of my sister's husband?

Are you having an affair with Paco? 

Am I on trial now?

No. I was working in fashion business and Roman Coppola saw pictures of me and I met Francis Ford Coppola and I was in Dracula. It was my first cameo but was so important for me because I realized that I wanted to be an actress. And then I went back to Rome and I started acting lessons and then I was in my first American film with a bigger role, of course. I was in Under Suspicion with Morgan Freeman and Gene Hackman. So I went to Los Angeles and they were so nice, so generous, and I felt completely welcome to the project.

## The Silent Language of Malèna

I went to Cannes festival and was trembling actually, I remember. And Gene Hackman touches me and he told me, you don't have to feel like that. I mean, you have to be relaxed, just go. And so he gave me the courage. 

Malèna speaks through the eyes and her body. It's a lot about body language and the body for actors is really an instrument, how to connect with the others. And in this film, it is really about that. Tornatore knew me because we did a commercial together and at that time he told me, "I have a story in my mind and if one day I'm going to make this movie, it's going to be with you." And he called me like three years later and he told me, you know, do you remember this project, Malèna? I want to make it. And we were shooting in Sicily for a few months and I love Sicily because I think that in Italy, without Sicily, we don't have cinemas because I think all the most beautiful stories, they come from Sicily.

## On Filming Violence and Societal Critique in Malèna

The sequence is very violent, but I have to say that those actresses, they were amazing with me. In the end, you know, nothing happened to me, even though the scene is very violent, of course. But we tried everything before, so I knew how to move without being in danger. And Tornatore was so protective as well. So actually, I was safe, even though the situation looks really, really terrible. But it gives the strength to the story. 

And this woman, Malèna, she's in a situation where the women hate her because she provoked desire and even the men, they don't protect her. And there is this scene that's so famous, you know, when she smokes the cigarette and all the men come closer. And actually, it's just about desire, nothing to do with love. We are in a male-dominated society, so a woman doesn't exist without a man. And so when she comes back in the end with her husband, at that moment, the people respect her again.

## The Choreographed Danger of 'Irréversible'

Irréversible is the most violent film I ever made. At the same time, it's also very poetic. It shows the beauty and monstrosity of human beings. Even in the scene that we all know that was very, you know, uh, dangerous—I mean, for the audience, it looks dangerous—but I was completely protected even in this one because it was like a choreography. So I knew every step I had to make. So it was like a dancing scene in some way. This film is also interesting the way it was made because there were 20 minutes long sequence shots. So I could act for 20 minutes nonstop like in theater. And this in cinema never happened. So, um, even the way it was made was something really special.

## Joining 'The Matrix' as Persephone

I'll give you what you want, but you have to give me something.

What?

A kiss.

Excuse me?

I want you to kiss me as if you were kissing her.

Why?

You love her, she loves you. It's all over you both.

When I did Dracula with Francis Ford Coppola, Keanu Reeves was in the film. So it was easier, it's always great when you know someone in a big cast like that. I felt more secure, you know, because I knew him already and he was very nice, very generous. And it was an experience. And Carrie-Anne Moss, she was so protective with me. And I was in Matrix Reloaded, Matrix Revolutions, so they all knew each other, so I was the new one. 

Persephone, she comes from a Greek mythology. In the Greek mythology, she's between hell and and human beings. She had to be, uh, secretive, mysterious, dangerous. At the same time, she needs love. She wants to feel uh, sensuality. So I had to play this character in a very elegant way.

## Playing Mary Magdalene in 'The Passion of the Christ'

When I did The Passion of Jesus Christ, I was in Rome at that time and I met the costume designer of the movie. I asked him, "Who is going to play Mary Magdalene?" I met Mel Gibson and he offered me the part. Mary Magdalene was such an incredible figure because to me, Mary Magdalene represents the humanity. Someone that is in front of something that is bigger than her and she can't explain because in the beginning, she doesn't have a faith. So she gets into that little by little. So to me, Mary Magdalene was such an interesting role because she represents the human condition.

## A Revolutionary Role in 'Spectre'

What a lovely view.

You're wasting your time. There are a hundred more that will come after me. 

All you buy me is five minutes.

Excellent. Time for a drink.

To be in a Bond movie is almost a secret dream for many actresses. And what happened to me was so funny because my agent called me and told me, "Monica, do you want to laugh? Sam Mendes wanted to meet you for James Bond." And I was 50 at the time. So I said, but he wants to meet me for M? I was, you know, because of course I was so happy to play M. I have so much respect for Dame Judy Dench. But he told me, "No, he wanted to meet you for a James Bond girl, Donna Lucia Sciarra, the oldest Bond lady ever."

Then you're obviously crazy, Mr. Bond.

James Bond.

To be in the movie for me at my age was a kind of revolutionary. And it was because this subject came out all the time—was there really something new that a mature woman could be close to James Bond? Also because Daniel Craig is younger than me. I mean, in reality, it proves that things are changing, and we are in a new era, and women have such an impact in society. And I think it's an example, this movie.

## Singing in 'Mozart in the Jungle'

The pasta was overcooked by at least three minutes. 

Four and a half. 

Well, I'm not here to conduct your cooking. And if my singing is overcooked, I will never allow that. Never.

Do you want to talk about the blood?

Well my heart, it has been bleeding for a while, and I think your voice is the only thing that can save it. 

Mozart in the Jungle is my first TV series and Roman Coppola produced this TV series. So it was such a beautiful coincidence to get in touch with him for the second time. In this TV series I had to play an opera singer completely obsessed with her voice, and she has this passionate love for a man who is younger than her, played by Gael García Bernal, who is a conductor. I had to sing in many different languages, so in German, Italian, English, and my sync had to be perfect. So I had to work very hard for this role. Alessandra was a woman that was suffering because she was losing her voice. So this instrument was so delicate and also she's scared of getting older. At the same time, what saves her is that she's very childish, and she comes out of the tragedy. She has this way to escape of the situations.

## Playing Herself in 'Call My Agent!'

You're beautiful. I want to share with you my life, my ranch, everything. 

When Marc Fitoussi, the French director, came to me with this project, I said, "Oh my God, what are you going to write down? It's about me." He told me, "No, it's going to be just an inspiration. Then of course the script is going to be bigger than life, so don't be scared. Go and let it go." And this is what I did. And actually was inspired by me as, you know, an actress, but at the same time I had to play someone who doesn't believe in love anymore. And was—but she wants an affair with her agent because she thinks he's the only one who can see her for who she is. It was really well written and so it was easy for me to play this role. I had so much fun. And also I was happy because I didn't have so many chances to play in comedies. You know, when you see all those films that we are talking about, Malèna and Under Suspicion and Irréversible, they're all so dramatic. So for me, it was so refreshing to be in a movie that was a comedy. My own dresses, different dresses, that I had really to give something of myself, not just the way I was acting. Because sometimes it's so interesting and important in our business to have some distance. And this role gave me the possibility to be distant of myself and also to play with myself and to laugh of myself as well. And I think sometimes it's important to do this.

## Inside Tim Burton's 'Beetlejuice Beetlejuice'

The dead, can they coexist? That's what we're here to find out, for a heap of truth.

Of course, I was a big fan of the first one and when Tim told me, "There is a key role in this movie and for which I thought about you," so I was very happy to accept it and to play it. Dolores, she's Beetlejuice's bride. The connection between them is that they have a dark side and they're connected by their soul. It's like poison love. Drama. Soon, my beloved. Soon.

What was incredible is that we didn't know each other and we had to play an intimate, funny scene right away. With him was easy because he was really generous and protective. And at the same time, it was so beautiful for me to see the relation through the years between Tim and Michael. And also what is so interesting in the film is to see all these actors that have grown with their characters and they still have fun to play those characters. An incredible honor to be part of this amazing cast and to enter into Tim's poetic, fantastic world. There is so much substance for an actor in his fairy tales.

## A Career Driven By Passion

It's the passion that drives you. And I believe in synergy. I mean, if you want something and you fight for it, things are going to happen.
